Protest classification: Broad-based uprising; not exclusively Gen Z
Main triggers and demands: Economic collapse; food and fuel shortages; inflation; corruption; demand for President Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s resignation.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Gotabaya Rajapaksa resigned in July 2022. A broad-based uprising, not an exclusively Gen Z movement.

Main triggers and demands: Proposed tax increases; cost of living; public debt; political corruption; accountability. Youth networks used digital platforms to coordinate demonstrations.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: President William Ruto withdrew the Finance Bill. Protests and demands for accountability returned in June 2025; concerns over police violence persisted.

Protest classification: Student-led; expanded into a broad national uprising
Main triggers and demands: Reinstatement of civil-service job quotas; perceived discrimination; unemployment; political repression; accountability.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled the country in August 2024. Longer-term reform demands remained contested.

Main triggers and demands: Novi Sad railway-station canopy collapse, which killed 16 people; demands for accountability, transparency and institutional reform.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Sustained mass protests and a political challenge ahead of the early parliamentary election scheduled for 25 October 2026.

Main triggers and demands: Justice over the 2023 train collision that killed 57 people; accountability for officials; improvements to rail safety.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Repeated mass demonstrations; demands for accountability continued. Not exclusively Gen Z.

Movement: Student protests after detention of Ekrem İmamoğlu
Main triggers and demands: Opposition to detention of Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu and revocation of his university diploma; democratic rights and academic freedom.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Arrests and police action were documented; student protests remained active in European Students’ Union monitoring in March–May 2026.

Main triggers and demands: Opposition to lawmakers’ housing allowances; economic inequality; inadequate education funding; police violence; death of motorcycle-taxi driver Affan Kurniawan intensified anger.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Protests spread across provinces with deadly clashes. Political parties agreed to reduce lawmakers’ benefits; protests in Jakarta were called off in early September amid security concerns.

Main triggers and demands: Social-media ban; corruption; nepotism; political privilege; unemployment; restrictions on free expression.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Prime Minister K. P. Sharma Oli resigned after deadly protests. An election followed in March 2026; broader reform demands require separate assessment.

Protest classification: Broad opposition/civil-society movement; youth participation not established as exclusive
Main triggers and demands: Opposition to a media regulation law; concerns about press freedom, corruption and democratic backsliding.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: The controversial law was enacted in September 2025 despite opposition. Protests subsequently subsided; the central demand for repeal was not achieved.

Main triggers and demands: Pension reform; crime and extortion; corruption scandals; opposition to President Dina Boluarte.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Congress removed Boluarte on 10 October 2025 amid wider political unrest. Security and accountability demands remained.

Protest classification: Youth- and student-involved; broad public participation
Main triggers and demands: Alleged corruption in public infrastructure projects; suspicious flood-control spending; calls for transparency.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Anti-corruption mobilization expanded beyond student groups. Investigations and accountability demands continued; a decisive resolution was not established in the reviewed sources.

Main triggers and demands: Water and electricity shortages; poverty; public-service failures; corruption; political accountability.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: President Andry Rajoelina fled the country in October 2025 amid the uprising and military defections. Subsequent transition raised questions about democratic civilian governance.

Main triggers and demands: Poor healthcare and education; youth unemployment; inadequate public services; perceived misplaced government spending.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Arrests and repression occurred, while the government promised more investment in health and education. The extent to which commitments satisfy demands remains contested.

Protest classification: Broader electoral uprising with substantial youth participation
Main triggers and demands: Alleged electoral irregularities; restricted political competition; accountability; opposition to the political establishment.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Demonstrations were met with a major crackdown. Allegations concerning the election and demands for accountability remained politically sensitive.

Protest classification: Gen Z-branded; wider participation and contested representation
Main triggers and demands: Cartel violence; insecurity; corruption; public anger after the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo on 1 November 2025.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Demonstrations occurred in multiple cities, with clashes and arrests. The government questioned the movement’s political independence; no equivalent national leadership change was established.

Main triggers and demands: Opposition to proposed tax and social-security increases in the 2026 budget; broader anger over corruption and political instability.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Prime Minister Rosen Zhelyazkov resigned on 11 December 2025 after sustained demonstrations. Not exclusively student-led.

Main triggers and demands: Opposition to federal immigration enforcement and treatment of migrants; concerns about government policy. High-school students organized walkouts and rallies.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Decentralized activism continued. Reporting cited an increase in student-led rallies even as wider pro-migrant demonstrations declined in February 2026; not one national Gen Z uprising.

Protest classification: Student activism; not a verified unified Gen Z uprising
Main triggers and demands: Student rights; university governance; education funding; international solidarity; wider social and political issues.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: European Students’ Union monitoring recorded UK student actions but did not isolate England in its published country totals. A nationwide England-specific Gen Z uprising was not established.

Main triggers and demands: Corruption allegations; unemployment; inadequate education; living costs; opposition to a controversial coastal development project.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Student demonstrations escalated into clashes in Tirana, with protesters demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation. Rama rejected calls to resign.

Main triggers and demands: Tuition costs; changes to Fees Free; higher-education funding; student allowances; student-union concerns.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Repeated student marches and strikes were documented at the University of Otago, including a rally of about 500 students on 29 July. No unified nationwide Gen Z uprising was established.

Movement: National student walkouts against One Nation
Main triggers and demands: High-school students protested against One Nation and its leader Pauline Hanson, with rallies in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and other locations.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Student-organized political demonstrations with hundreds participating in major cities; not a national anti-government uprising.

Movement: High-school student protests and broader social unrest
Main triggers and demands: Underfunded schools; teacher shortages; school conditions; university admissions; rising living costs; wider economic grievances.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Mass demonstrations and serious clashes were reported in October, with arrests and scrutiny of police conduct. Reporting also described promised additional teachers and reversal of planned university fee increases; wider grievances remained contested.

Protest classification: Broad-based social movement with youth participation
Main triggers and demands: Rising rents; evictions; lack of affordable housing; demands for rent controls and eviction protections.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Demonstrations and housing activism continued; not an exclusively student-led or Gen Z uprising.

Movement: Student march to defend public education
Main triggers and demands: Education-budget cuts; reduced public investment; pressure on employment and social services.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Students and education supporters demonstrated before debate on the 2027 budget. The dispute over education funding remained unresolved at the time of reporting.

Main triggers and demands: Student fees; high accommodation costs; cost-of-living pressures; insufficient student housing.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: More than 1,500 students marched in Dublin according to RTÉ. Organizers called for education funding and affordable accommodation.

Movement: Cockroach Janta Party and youth-led protests
Main triggers and demands: Exam-paper leaks; unemployment; education grievances; allegations of electoral irregularities; demands for the Election Commission chief’s resignation.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Protests intensified in October, with arrests and judicial custody for movement leaders reported on 19 October. The Election Commission disputed allegations surrounding voter-roll removals.

Movement: Student activism amid wider European unrest
Protest classification: Student activism intersecting with broader demonstrations
Main triggers and demands: Education and public-service concerns; economic insecurity; government policy; broader political grievances and living costs.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Demonstrations and clashes were reported in October. Student actions should be distinguished from other groups; no national Gen Z-led political transition was established.

Movement: Student and youth demonstrations amid European unrest
Main triggers and demands: Education funding; tuition and higher-education reforms; wider grievances about living costs and public services.
Status / outcome as of 2026-10-20: Protests and clashes were reported in Brussels and Liège amid wider European unrest. Specific education-policy outcomes remained uncertain.
